To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the ICRH wave power deposition in the minority ions is strongly dependent on the plasma parameters and on the ICRH antenna loading, and (ii) the ICRF heating of the minority ions can be used to drive EPM instabilities in a wide range of parameters, and to control them through the ICRH power.

the quasi-linear ICRH wave-particle interaction is able to accelerate minority deuterons up to energies of 10-20 MeV in FAST and 30-50 MeV in ITER; the fast ion distribution function is peaked in the central part of the plasma and has a significant anisotropy; the fast ion pressure gradient drives a significant Alfvénic instability below the EPM threshold; the Alfvénic activity is strongly reduced when the EPM instability is saturated;

the ICRH heating scheme in the ITER-like regime is capable of accelerating a sufficient fraction of the minority ions to the energy range of interest for addressing burning plasma physics issues and that the ICRF heating efficiency in this regime is high enough to make the ICRH a promising candidate for the heating and current drive scheme in ITER.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following topics: (1) ICRH wave propagation, (2) quasi-linear fast ion acceleration by ICRH, (3) fast ion driven instabilities, (4) cross-scale couplings between energetic particles and micro-turbulence, (5) ICRH fast ion transport, and (6) fast ion confinement.
the following topics: (i) The study of fast ion transport and confinement by the analysis of the quasi- linear plasma-ICRH interaction, which is based on the use of a 1D Fokker-Planck code.
the investigation of the ICRH fast ion acceleration and transport in the presence of Alfvénic instabilities, which are the main source of fast ion loss in burning plasmas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the ICRH scheme is a very powerful tool to address some of the most relevant ITER burning plasma physics topics.
the ICRH heating scheme is a powerful tool for the investigation of burning plasma physics.

the ICRH scheme can be a powerful tool to investigate burning plasma physics issues in the future tokamaks, such as the ITER, if the ICRH system is optimized to produce energetic ions with a high enough density and temperature, and a low enough pitch angle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ICRH is a very powerful tool for addressing burning plasma issues in ITER.
the FAST design, which is based on the ICRH as the main heating scheme, can provide a unique opportunity for investigating burning plasma physics issues in a realistic ITER-like scenario.
the FAST ICRH system is a promising tool for addressing the main burning plasma physics issues.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ICRH heating scheme can provide a very efficient way to produce a high energetic ion density in the core of the burning plasma and, at the same time, to control the EPM stability threshold.
the FAST ICRH system can be used to address the burning plasma physics issues mentioned above.
, with the ICRH power available in ITER, the fast ion population can be made large enough to drive EPM instabilities and thus to investigate the burning plasma physics issues mentioned above.
